sections.h2: What written notice does a Kentucky landlord have to give before an eviction?
sections.html:
It depends on the reason and on where the rental sits. Kentucky lets cities, counties and urban-county governments adopt the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA), KRS 383.505 to 383.715, and the notice periods in that act apply only where a local government has adopted it. Everywhere else, older rules in KRS Chapter 383 govern.

A 2017 legislative estimate counted 33 cities as adopters, with Lexington-Fayette and Louisville-Jefferson among them, and it said Oldham and Pulaski counties had also adopted. No current list was available to the writers of that estimate, so ask the city or county clerk whether the URLTA is in force where your house is.

sections.h2: Which notice periods apply in Kentucky?
sections.html:
The table gathers the periods in the statutes, with the type of tenancy that triggers each one. Every notice should be in writing and should state the reason and the date the tenancy ends.

Written notice periods in KRS Chapter 383
SituationNoticeStatute
Unpaid rent where the URLTA applies7 days after notice of nonpayment and intent to terminateKRS 383.660(2)
Other material breach where the URLTA appliesTermination date at least 14 days after receipt, breach not cured in 15 daysKRS 383.660(1)
Week-to-week tenancy7 days before the termination dateKRS 383.695(1)
Month-to-month tenancy30 days before the periodic rental dateKRS 383.695(2)
Tenancy continuing after a written lease ends10 days, or none if rent is 10 days lateKRS 383.695(3)
Tenancy at will or by sufferance where the URLTA is not in effectOne monthKRS 383.195
Unapproved transfer of the tenancy by a short-term tenant10 days to quitKRS 383.180(2)

sections.h2: How many days does a tenant get to pay overdue rent?
sections.html:
Where the URLTA applies, the tenant gets seven days after written notice that rent is unpaid and that the landlord intends to end the tenancy. If the tenant pays inside that window, the landlord has no ground to terminate.

A landlord who takes rent after learning of a default can lose the right to terminate for that default. KRS 383.675 says accepting rent with knowledge of a default, or accepting performance that differs from the agreement, waives the right to end the tenancy for that breach unless the parties agree otherwise afterward. Landlords who plan to sell should decide early whether they will accept partial payments.

sections.h2: What notice covers a lease violation other than rent?
sections.html:
For a material breach where the URLTA is in force, the landlord delivers a written notice that names the acts or omissions and sets a termination date at least 14 days after the tenant receives it. If the breach is not remedied within 15 days, the agreement ends as the notice states.

  • A breach that can be fixed by repairs or payment of damages ends the matter if the tenant fixes it before the date in the notice.
  • If substantially the same act or omission returns within six months, the landlord may terminate on at least 14 days of written notice without offering a new chance to cure.
  • A willful holdover after termination can cost the tenant up to three months of periodic rent or threefold actual damages, whichever is greater, plus reasonable attorney's fees, but only when the holdover is willful and not in good faith.

sections.h2: What happens where the URLTA has not been adopted?
sections.html:
Older provisions take over. A tenancy at will or by sufferance ends on one month's written notice to remove, and a tenant who stays past the end of a fixed term can be removed on a short timeline if the landlord moves quickly.

  • Term of a year or more: the tenant gets no right to stay for 90 days after expiry, and possession can be recovered without demand or notice if proceedings begin inside that time.
  • Term under a year: the same rule runs for 30 days.
  • If the landlord waits past those windows, no proceeding is allowed until a later period passes, and the tenancy then continues as before.

Check the local ordinance too. The statute bars a city or county from passing any other ordinance on the subjects covered by the URLTA, but local rules can still exist outside those subjects.

sections.h2: How must a Kentucky eviction notice be delivered?
sections.html:
Under the URLTA, a tenant receives notice when it is delivered in hand, or mailed by registered or certified mail to the place the tenant designated, or to the last known residence if none was designated. A landlord receives notice at the business address used for the rental agreement or by certified mail to that place.

Keep a copy of the notice, the mailing receipt and a dated note of how it was delivered. The date of receipt starts the 14-day period, so a mailed notice should allow time for delivery before any deadline is calculated.

sections.h2: What is a landlord forbidden to do during the notice period?
sections.html:
A landlord may not take possession by self-help. KRS 383.690 bars recovering the dwelling by action or otherwise, including cutting heat, electric, running water, hot water, gas or another essential service, except on abandonment, surrender or as the URLTA permits.

Retaliation is also barred. KRS 383.705 stops a landlord from raising rent, cutting services or threatening an action for possession after a tenant complains to a housing code agency, complains to the landlord about a covered violation, or joins a tenant organization. A complaint within one year before the alleged retaliation creates a presumption of retaliation, but the landlord may still sue when the tenant is behind on rent.

sections.h2: Can a Kentucky tenant also give notice to end a tenancy?
sections.html:
Yes. KRS 383.695 says the landlord or the tenant may end a week-to-week tenancy with seven days of written notice and a month-to-month tenancy with 30 days of written notice before the periodic rental date. The same section lets either side end a tenancy that began when a written lease ended on 10 days of written notice.

For a landlord preparing to sell, a tenant's own notice can solve a vacancy question without any court case. Put the tenant's notice in the file with its date, and confirm the move-out date in writing so there is no dispute about when the keys come back.

sections.h2: How does a notice interact with selling a rented house in Kentucky?
sections.html:
A sale does not cancel the tenancy. KRS 383.600 relieves a landlord who conveys the premises in a good faith sale to a bona fide purchaser of liability under the rental agreement for events after written notice of the conveyance to the tenant, unless the parties agreed otherwise.

Showings need advance notice. KRS 383.615 requires at least two days' notice before entering to exhibit the unit to prospective purchasers, at reasonable times, except in an emergency. Tenants may not unreasonably withhold consent.

  • Decide whether to sell with the tenant in place or finish the notice first.
  • Tell the tenant about the sale in writing once the contract is signed.
  • Ask the closing attorney how the lease passes to the buyer and who holds the security deposit.

faqs.q: How many days notice must a Kentucky landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven days where the URLTA applies. The landlord gives written notice of nonpayment and of the intent to terminate, and the tenant has seven days to pay before the landlord may end the tenancy.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Kentucky?
faqs.a: Thirty days of written notice before the periodic rental date, under KRS 383.695(2). Outside URLTA areas, a tenancy at will or by sufferance ends on one month's written notice.

faqs.q: Can a Kentucky landlord evict without any notice?
faqs.a: Rarely. After a written lease ends and the tenant stays, rent unpaid 10 days after it was due lets the landlord end the tenancy without notice under KRS 383.695(3). In other cases a written notice comes first.

faqs.q: Can a landlord change the locks or shut off utilities to force a tenant out?
faqs.a: No. KRS 383.690 forbids recovering possession by cutting off heat, electric, water, gas or other essential service, except on abandonment or surrender.

faqs.q: Does selling the house end the lease?
faqs.a: Not by itself. KRS 383.600 relieves the seller of liability for later events once the tenant has written notice of the conveyance, unless the parties agreed otherwise. Read the lease and the sale contract to see what happens to the tenancy.
